title.en: Lay out a circuit so the flow is readable

summary: Keep a consistent flow direction, disambiguate crossings and junctions, and use depth only where it clarifies.
objective: Make a spatial circuit or graph legible enough that structure can be read without tracing every line.
applies_when: A circuit, dataflow graph or network is arranged spatially.
Connections cross, branch or fan out.
A three-dimensional layout is being considered for a fundamentally planar diagram.
example_prompts: Lay out the adder so the carry chain is easy to follow.
Make the connections readable without a tangle.
negative_signals: Deliberately chaotic or artistic network imagery.
Physical layouts where the geometry is dictated by a real board or device.
not_for: Deliberately chaotic or artistic network imagery.
Physical layouts where the geometry is dictated by a real board or device.

principles: Convention carries information cheaply. A consistent left-to-right or bottom-to-top flow lets a viewer read direction without arrowheads on every segment.
Crossings and junctions are the main source of misreading. A branch and a crossing look identical unless the junction is marked or the crossing is bridged.

Depth in three dimensions solves occlusion badly: lines at different depths appear to cross from most angles, so a third axis should carry meaning such as stage, layer or time rather than being used to spread a planar graph.
Layout stability matters across edits: if positions change every time the circuit is modified, the viewer loses the mental map they had built.
implementation: Order elements by logical depth along the flow axis, so a signal never has to travel backwards without a visible reason.
Mark junctions explicitly and route crossings to be visually distinct, for example with a jog or a bridge.
If a third axis is used, bind it to a meaningful quantity such as bit position, pipeline stage or hierarchy level, and label it.
Keep positions stable under edits by anchoring the layout to identities rather than recomputing a free layout each time.
Provide a hover or selection mode that highlights a whole net, which handles the residual ambiguity of any layout.
observable_checks: Trace one signal end to end using the interaction the design actually offers. In a static diagram that must work without interaction; in a layout that deliberately relies on hover or selection highlighting, test that the highlight resolves the ambiguity quickly and consistently rather than counting any click as a failure.
Rotate a three-dimensional layout and confirm that apparent crossings do not change the reading, which tests whether depth is doing real work.
Add an element and confirm existing positions remain recognisable.
Check that every junction is distinguishable from a crossing at the intended zoom level.

creative_affordances: Stylised, sculptural or physical-object circuit presentations remain valid when flow and junctions stay legible.
Deliberately dense layouts can be an aesthetic choice if a highlight mode provides the reading path.
known_limits: Authored composition guidance; it cites no perceptual study and no layout algorithm is prescribed.
No runtime layout has been evaluated for this record.
